correctness.rationale: For a unit direction the length is min(2a/√(1−U_z²),2b/√(1−U_x²)). Let R=√(a²+b²). The absolute coordinate marginals are uniform; the signed pair projects to the unit disk with density 1/(2π√(1−z²−x²)). Hence the central-band overlap is (2/π)∫₀ˢ arcsin(t/√(1−z²)) dz when s²+t²<1. Integration by parts followed by z=√(1−t²)sin φ gives the stated elementary expression. Below 2b only the a-constraint has positive probability of limiting the chord at the threshold; at 2R the strict absolute-coordinate survival inequalities cannot both hold, and equality is attained at |U_x|=a/R, |U_z|=b/R. Every interior length is attained by continuity. There are no atoms. On the interior two-constraint branch, conditioning on |U_z|=s or on |U_x|=t and differentiating its marginal threshold gives the two joint length/contact densities, since ties have spherical measure zero. The factors in brackets can be written as (2/π)arctan(√Δ/t) and (2/π)arctan(√Δ/s), respectively, with Δ=4R²/l²−1. Thus as l=2R−ε, the densities are asymptotic to a√Δ/(πRb) and b√Δ/(πRa), giving the limiting proportions and, on integrating their sum, 2√R ε^(3/2)/(3πab). At 2b the first marginal changes by O(ε); the second opens with t∼√(ε/b), multiplied by 1−(2/π)arcsin(√(1−a²/b²))=(2/π)arcsin(a/b). The lower endpoint follows directly from s∼√(ε/a). This independently fills in the abbreviated upper-tail calculation. The supplied numerical checker was inspected, not executed; no Monte Carlo evidence is needed for these identities.
